sentences: A group homomorphism preserves the group operation when mapping elements from one group to another.
The standard homomorphism tester samples two elements and checks whether the function respects their product.
The question asks for the smallest possible rejection probability among functions at each feasible distance from the nearest homomorphism, for every pair of groups.
The saved 2017 textbook records gaps even in the special case of Boolean linearity testing and distinguishes the exact curve from its known lower bounds.
A sharp analysis would clarify this fundamental local test and strengthen understanding of a tool used in probabilistically checkable proof constructions.
